title: Living Business Card order
description: One paid card order, filled in by a person from the Stripe payment and the buyer's answers. Never holds payment data (no card numbers, Stripe IDs or amounts). build_order.py checks every rule here and refuses the order, naming each problem, when anything is missing or wrong. Nothing is filled in by default.

order_ref.description: Our reference for the order, written on the proof and the folder. Letters, numbers and dashes only.

tier.description: ready-made (AUD 249): one of the nine ready-made films. made-for-you (AUD 449): a custom film, made after the proof.

film.description: ready-made: the name of one of the nine ready-made films. made-for-you: exactly "custom, pending proof".

buyer_name.description: The buyer's name exactly as it should show on the card and in the saved contact.

role.description: One short line under the name, for example "Owner, Sample Plumbing Co".

email.description: The email the card shows and the saved contact carries.

phone.description: The phone the card shows, or null when the buyer asked for no phone on the card. The key must be there either way.

businesses.description: Every business on the card. The first is the main business; each one after it is an extra business (AUD 199 each).

url.description: Plain https, no spaces, quotes or angle brackets.

note.description: Optional short line under the business, for example "Plumbing, Brisbane".

extra_businesses.description: How many extra businesses were paid for. Must equal the number of businesses after the first.

logo_file.description: Path to the buyer's own logo as a PNG (at most 120000 bytes, about 256 px; re-export a JPEG to PNG first). Relative paths are read from the order file's folder. It is the card's logo and the saved contact's picture.

brand_colour.description: Optional. The buyer's own main colour as #RRGGBB, from their logo or website. Left out means the proof lists it as not yet supplied.

colour_source.description: Required with brand_colour: where the colour came from, for example "measured from the buyer's logo".
